plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, paying only that second-highest bid, which guarantees non-negative profit whenever you win and maximizes expected profit overall. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks losses. With value $30, the optimal action is to bid exactly $30, ensuring truthful revelation and optimal expected payoff given the uniform distribution of competitors' values.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding my true value of $28 maximizes my expected profit—I won't overpay since payment is determined by the second-highest bid, and bidding higher or lower than my value only reduces my expected profit or winning chances without benefit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies, since you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks winning at a loss. With my value at $22, the optimal action is to bid exactly $22 to maximize expected profit.
